Subject: Next steps: deployment & security checklist for Northstar PoC

Hi Avery —

Thanks again for the call earlier today. Quick recap from our side and a few asks so we can scope the PoC and prepare for our upcoming compliance review: 

- High level: We want to run a 6-week PoC with a single Northstar EHR integration, processing de-identified patient notes initially, then a small set of PHI records for validation. Estimated peak TPS: ~12 requests/sec, average payload ~2kb.
- Primary decision drivers: HIPAA/BAA coverage, SOC2 evidence, data residency (US only), and the ability to supply audit evidence for our external auditor (scheduled Aug 20).

Can you confirm the following items so we can confirm internal budget and timeline?
1) Which deployment mode you recommend for the PoC given our need to show isolated environments for audit (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC/on-prem) and why.
2) A list of security artifacts Redwood can provide (SOC2 Type II report or summary, encryption at rest/in transit details, key management options, network topology diagram).
3) Whether you can provide a BAA template we can start redlining and an estimate of legal’s typical turnaround.
4) Any constraints on ability to mirror production network flows for the auditor (e.g., can we run a short security walkthrough with an engineer and a network diagram?).

We have attached a short spreadsheet with expected volumes and a preliminary timeline.

Attachments: [Attachment: PoC_volume_estimate.xlsx (stated)]

If you can send a recommended mutual action plan and any gaps, we’ll share with our security and legal teams this afternoon.

Best,
Alicia Gomez
Head of Clinical Ops
Northstar Clinics

From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Gomez <agomez@northstarclinics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Tom Reed <treed@northstarclinics.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 18:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Next steps: deployment & security checklist for Northstar PoC

Hi Alicia — thanks for the clear recap and the spreadsheet, that helps. Short answers up front and a proposed MAP below. I added Marissa (solutions) and Sean (security) to help own technical and compliance items.

1) Recommendation: For the PoC I typically recommend Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pool) for customers who want isolated runtime and predictable performance without the heavier lift of a Private VPC. Dedicated gives you environment isolation (no multi-tenant mixing), VPC peering options, and straightforward evidence for auditors. If your external auditor insists on customer-controlled network boundaries or an air-gapped setup, we can discuss Private (VPC or on-prem) but that will add ~4–8 weeks of setup and legal work.

2) Security artifacts we can provide immediately: SOC2 summary report (we can provide redacted Type II on NDA), SOC2 attest letter, encryption-at-rest/in-transit details, KMS integration options (Cloud KMS / customer-managed keys), and a network diagram. We will attach the SOC2 summary and network diagram to this thread.

3) BAA: attached is our standard BAA draft. Legal turnaround is usually 7–14 business days for standard redlines; expedited review (3–5 bd) can be requested for PoC customers.

4) Security walkthrough: yes — Sean can run a 60–90 minute security call next week and provide an audit manifest for your external auditor (list of logs, retention, access records).

Proposed Mutual Action Plan (high level):
- Jul 15: Security walkthrough with Sean (60m) — confirm artifact list and auditor needs.
- Jul 16: Redwood shares SOC2 summary, network diagram, BAA draft (attached).
- Jul 19: Northstar returns redlines on BAA + confirmation of PoC scope (payloads/sample data).
- Jul 21: Provision Dedicated environment + initial integration (estimated 3–5 business days to be up).
- Jul 28: Run first integration test with de-identified data; collect logs and prepare evidence package.

We can flex timelines if you prefer to start on Hosted to accelerate functional validation, but that path will not satisfy isolation requirements for an external audit. Happy to talk tradeoffs on cost vs risk on the walkthrough.

Attachments: [Attachment: SOC2_summary.pdf (2 pages)] [Attachment: BAA_draft.docx (template)] [Attachment: Network_Diagram.png]

Thanks — I’ll loop Sean for the walkthrough scheduling.

— Avery Johnson
Business Development Lead, Redwood Inference

On Wed, Jul 14, 2026 at 6:04 PM Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Provisional MAP listed below — Sean will lead the security walkthrough.

Hi Alicia, quick technical notes from the solutions side to help you decide between Dedicated and Private: 

- Dedicated pros: environment isolation, predictable throughput, easier to stand up quickly (3–5 business days), supports VPC peering + customer-managed KMS, full token-level logging and per-route observability. Cost: mid-range for a small reserved pool; we can provide a cost estimate once we lock expected qps and sequence lengths.
- Private (VPC/on-prem) pros: customer-controlled network boundaries, best for auditors that require customer-owned network segments or no external routing. Cons: longer lead time (4–8 weeks), some operational work from your infra team (routing, KMS access), and higher baseline cost.

Other items we’ll prepare for the walkthrough: a short evidence manifest (what logs / time ranges auditors typically request), a sample integration checklist for the EHR adapter, and an example test plan for PHI validation.

Action items for our side (we’ll bring these to the walkthrough):
- Provide SOC2 summary and attest letter.
- Share network diagram and sample audit manifest.
- Draft cost estimate for Dedicated pool sized to your numbers in the spreadsheet.

Would you be available for the walkthrough on Jul 16 at 10:00am PT or Jul 17 at 2:00pm PT? If you prefer, we can do a 30-minute pre-call for legal to triage the BAA redlines.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
